lore_anchors.definition: A magically binding promise sworn to the universe itself. Breaking a Dao Oath results in catastrophic karmic backlash, often causing instant death or cultivation collapse. It is a powerful tool for binding allies or enemies to a specific course of action.

A grand formation that manifests as floating mountain peaks and generates a chaotic True Fire of mixed elemental power. It is a devastating siege weapon, capable of threatening even Celestial Immortals.

The original, primordial world from which the current Three Realms were formed after its destruction. Beings from this world, like the Xia Emperor, are considered to have deep, ancient lineages and hidden powers.

A supreme Daofather-level being from Chinese mythology, associated with the Yinglong (a winged dragon). In this universe, he is a major power in the Three Realms and a sworn brother of the Grand Xia Emperor.

One of the many Major Worlds within a Realmverse. Unlike the unified and relatively peaceful Grand Xia World, the Beishan Major World is a chaotic battlefield, making it a dangerous posting for any cultivator.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why did Buchasi kill the entire Donglin Sect?
cultural_notes_faq.a: He did it to eliminate all witnesses to his failure and to clean up his compromised base. It was a brutal but efficient security protocol to prevent the organization's secrets from leaking further.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why didn't the Cave Master execute Buchasi?
cultural_notes_faq.a: Because Ji Ning swore a Dao Oath not to reveal the secret of the puppet castle. Since the core secret was likely safe, Buchasi's failure was a serious but not capital offense.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why are the invaders so cautious about the Grand Xia World?
cultural_notes_faq.a: They fear the hidden background of the Xia Emperor, who is from the ancient imperial clan of the Primordial Pangu World, and his sworn brother, the incredibly powerful Daofather Yinglong.
